judgements.justification: A's spotlight at a 7.0 mean, where 32 of 44 copies got a poster, came from the area chair's own reading; its five-sentence meta-review gives no reason beyond its own view that 'it is nice work' with broad potential.

A's area chair rested the spotlight on SMI having 'the potential to become a very useful tool ... and may thus have broad impact', which the paper's proof-of-concept experiments do not show; B's area chair made no such forecast.
No score is known to have moved after the rebuttal in either committee; reviewers in both said they were satisfied and kept their scores.

A's theory scrutiny was thin: champion Reviewer_imZu (8, 3.5 h) called the theory 'sound' without specifics, and Reviewer_C7hP (3 h) did not check the math; B's reviewers found three conceded errors A missed.

Only B found the Proposition 1 independence error, the dimension dependence hidden in C and M, and the misleading DPI argument; these held CzLh at 6 and B's area chair made the DPI fix a condition of acceptance.

Both committees saw the missing MI-estimator baselines and proof-of-concept-only experiments; A's reviewers gave 6 to 7 and called benchmarks 'probably out of scope', while B's Reviewer_eiQW rated 4 on them.
CzLh and 6PJ4 took up the DPI point after reading other reviews, but neither changed a score.
No reviewer's rating clearly contradicts their own text; eiQW's 4 matches its critique and CzLh's 6 matches its remaining reservations.
Reviewer_C7hP admitted unchecked math but rated 7, not a borderline default; no committee's mean was held near the threshold by unsure reviewers.
Neither area chair adopted a lone outlying reviewer's verdict; A's followed unanimous support and B's set eiQW aside.
The committees' verbal assessments differ in substance (B found theory errors A did not), so the score gap is not a calibration gap on similar verdicts.
A's unanimity included an 8, above the accept level, and B's mean (6.0) and maximum (7) were lower, so the definition's conditions do not hold.
No score is recorded as rising on rebuttal material in either committee.

A's meta-review weighs no criticism, dropping Reviewer_dcfo's doubt on practical significance and the shared request for MI-estimator baselines, while B's meta-review carried its reviewers' DPI reservation forward as a condition.

A's Reviewer_C7hP rated originality high on the misreading that SMI is 'a new estimator of the mutual information', and B's Reviewer_eiQW's 4 partly rests on the wrong claims that DV is the main estimator and that no dimension sweep exists.
B's concessions (mutual independence, dimension in C and M, DPI wording) kept B at a poster, and A heard no damaging admission; A's authors denied dcfo's low-dimension point instead.
No objection or score cut came after the response period; the DPI point raised in B's 2021-08-31 comments had already been raised by GPCD and answered.
The score profiles are not near-identical (means 7.0 and 6.0), so different tier cut-offs do not explain the split.
B's area chair passed over eiQW, but eiQW's review mixes correct points with misreads and is not B's most specific review; GPCD and CzLh were better informed on the theory.
Neither committee's scores moved on the rebuttal, so no difference in what the rebuttal could answer lifted one committee further.
B's lone detractor Reviewer_eiQW (4 against 7, 6, 7) pulls B's mean from 6.67 to 6.0, a mean at which none of 89 copies got a spotlight; B's other three scores are close to A's 6, 7, 7, 8.
Reviewer_eiQW, B's outlier, neither edited nor replied after the authors answered its DV and dimension points, so its 4 stood unrevised.
B's area chair did not discard eiQW as unreliable or defend acceptance against it; it called the reviews 'overwhelmingly positive' and followed the mean.

reasoning: The split has two parts, and existing reasons cover both. A's spotlight at a 7.0 mean was the area chair's own upgrade on a forecast of broad impact, with no criticism weighed (R01, R02, R14). B's mean was lower because its reviewers read the theory more closely and found three conceded errors that A's thin reviews missed (R04, R05), and because B's lone detractor weighed the shared experimental gap heavily, partly on misreads, and never answered the rebuttal (R06, R15, R21, R22). The stage 1 candidates (AC upgrade, lone detractor, weighting, closer theory reading, DPI framing, thin champion) all map to existing reasons, so no reason is added.
